items.text: REFERRED TO CIVIL SERVICE AND PENSIONS

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation
to first grade firefighters and promotions from the firefighter rank
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S9202

SPONSOR: JACKSON
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in
relation to first grade firefighters and promotions from the firefighter
rank

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of this bill would amend section 15-110 of the administrative
code of the City of New York to provide that when a member of the New
York City Fire Department accrues twenty-five years of service and
retires in any rank, an amount equal to five percent of the highest
grade of pay under the applicable collective bargaining agreement for
the rank in which the member retires shall be added to the salary used
to calculate such member's pension benefits under the New York City Fire
Department Pension Fund.

Section 2 of this bill would provide that beginning with the twenty-
sixth year of service, and for each year of service thereafter, the
member shall receive an additional one percent increase annually in the
salary used for pension calculation purposes. This additional credit
shall not exceed a total of fifteen percent and shall be capped upon
completion of thirty-five years of uniformed service with the depart-
ment.

Section 3 of this bill provides for the effective date of the act.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This legislation serves to strengthen recruitment and retention efforts
by offering incentives that encourage experienced uniformed firefighters
and other uniformed ranks of the fire department to continue their
public service. Keeping seasoned members in these ranks on the job
directly enhances public safety, as their knowledge and expertise would
provide critical guidance and mentorship to younger members of the
department. Pension-related benefit costs for new hires typically exceed
the pension costs associated with present-day retirees. This legislation
would mitigate the impact of pension liabilities, while maximizing the
City's prior investment in training and development of members to serve
in these ranks, through this enhanced recruitment and retention. More-
over, while reducing pension expenses that put a strain on the City's
budget, this legislation would also assist in maintaining adequate
staffing levels.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

See Fiscal Note.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This Act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Provides for longevity bonuses relating to first grade firefighters and promotions from the firefighter rank.
